16.0.s.en: 1. The family, an icon of heaven

16.0.0.en: 1 Do not desire a multitude of children who are no good, and do not rejoice in hypocritical sons, and do not delight in their multitude, if the fear of the Lord is not in them. 2 Do not trust in their life, and look not to their place. 3 One child who fears the Lord is better than a thousand hypocrites. 4 And to die without a child is better than hypocritical children. 5 For by one sensible man a city is peopled, and a tribe of the lawless is laid waste.

16.0.1.en: Do not desire a multitude of useless children, and do not rejoice in wicked sons [1].

16.0.2.en: As he presents to us God's dealings with sinners who chose to practice sin at the expense of our love for God and our keeping of the divine commandment, why did he begin by speaking of not being preoccupied with the multitude of sons but with raising them and sanctifying them as befits the people of the holy God? He began with the children for two reasons:

16.0.3.en: The first reason: the normal person - even the unbeliever - longs to see his children successful in life, advancing in learning and knowledge, loved by society, enjoying good health and length of days more than he. Many wish that whatever diseases befall one of their children might befall themselves and their children be healed. Therefore when the Lord warned His people against sin He made clear that its consequences extend into the lives of their children and grandchildren, so the fruits of sin extend to children and grandchildren, not in order to blame or repay the children, but that the fathers may cease from sin out of love for their children! It is said: "visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me" (Ex 20:5).

16.0.4.en: The second reason: a person feels that his children are a divine gift, especially in the Old Testament. For a multitude of children was a sign of the blessing of the Lord (Gen 24:60; Ps 128:3-6). And in the New Testament a multitude of children according to the Spirit is looked upon as a divine blessing, for when they have little children who bear witness to the Gospel the fathers sing: "Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me" (Heb 2:13). Therefore Ben Sirach warns us of useless or wicked children who have no share in the Kingdom of Heaven.

16.0.5.en: The psalmist says: "Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward" (Ps 127:3). The Hebrews counted sons a blessing from the Lord: "Blessed shall be the fruit of thy body" (Deut 28:4), "and the LORD shall make thee plenteous in goods, in the fruit of thy body" (Deut 28:11). If sons according to the flesh are a gift from the Lord, then all the more the sons who enjoy the grace of adoption as children of God are a gift of the Lord that He gives to the Church as a fruitful mother, as St. Augustine says.

16.0.6.en: And St. Jerome sees that the wife, the bride who bears many blessed children, is wisdom, for he says that the wife and children must be understood spiritually, otherwise we would imagine that the angels do not enjoy such blessings, because they have neither wives nor children. Who then is the spiritual wife? Solomon longed that wisdom be a wife to him (Prov 4:6, 8).

16.0.7.en: v Let us also take her as a wife for ourselves, and let us embrace her (Eccl 2:8). Let us not let her depart from our embrace, nor flee from between our arms. For if that bride is always in our bosom, we shall beget children from her... I mean what he says here: "Thy children like olive plants round about thy table"... For he who takes wisdom as a wife begets children from her...

16.0.8.en: Just as the vine bears many clusters and has one root, and spreads its branches in breadth and flourishing... so wisdom, who is our wife, if we do not let her leave us, brings forth in us many clusters, that is, many virtues, and a strong holy will and many noble works [1].

16.1.0.en: St. Jerome v His wife here is said concerning Christ, and she is the Church. His wife is us, "as a fruitful vine" [2].

16.2.0.en: v The Church also, our beloved mother, bears good sons. Consider how she bears. She bears by baptism, which is the womb of the Church, so that everyone who wishes to be born again enters his mother's womb a second time and is born from her. This miracle Nicodemus, the teacher of Israel, was not able to understand [3].

16.2.1.en: St. Augustine If their number is multiplied do not rejoice, if the fear of the Lord is not in them [2].

16.3.0.en: v Do not care about their number, for one man who fears God is better than a thousand wicked, as the Lord said by the prophet [4].

16.3.1.en: St. Cyprian the Martyr v Few, in truth, come to be counted in the number who are rich in virtue. Say: What use is it if there is much straw when there ought to be precious stones? Number is not counted in a mass but in what is approved. Elijah was one, and yet the whole world was not worthy of what he deserved. The world contains myriads, but they are not myriads when they do not reach to this one. One who does the will of God is better than ten thousand disobedient. For the ten thousand have not yet reached to this one.

16.3.2.en: "Do not desire a multitude of children who are no good" (cf. Sir 16:1)... What did he gain from this crowd? They are rather food for the fires. This can be seen by a person even in the body, for moderate food with health is better than a fat ox with ruin. This food is more than the other. The first is food, and the second is disease.

16.4.0.en: This also we see in war, for ten experienced and courageous men are better than ten thousand without experience. The latter, besides not working, hinder even those who work [5].

16.4.1.en: St. John Chrysostom Do not rely on their (long) life, nor lean on their number.

16.4.2.en: One pious child is better than a thousand, and to die without begetting is better than to have wicked children [3].

16.4.3.en: Proper upbringing of children: St. John Chrysostom often spoke of the upbringing of children, which he considers a holy work. What concerned him in their upbringing was neither the outward appearance nor boasting of their temporal success. On the other hand, neglecting their upbringing is considered a grave crime that exceeds the cruelty of the pagan barbarians.

16.5.0.en: v The cruelty of the barbarians only brings their enemies down to slavery with the ruin of their city and its enslavement and grievous assault with bodily torments. But you bring (your children) down to the slavery of souls, binding them with fetters like slaves, and offering them as prey to the wicked, savage demons and to their lusts. In truth you give them no spiritual counsel, and you leave no room for others to perform this duty; your conduct is altogether different [6].

16.5.1.en: v This obligation belongs to fathers as well as to mothers. There are fathers who sacrifice everything in order to secure for their children teachers for the enjoyment of pleasures, and make of them wealthy heirs. But that the children become Christians and practice godliness, they care little about this. What blindness that is counted a crime!

16.5.2.en: It is an absurd negligence, responsible for the confusion that makes society bitter. Suppose you prepare great possessions for them. If they do not know how to conduct themselves in their lives, then these possessions will surely not last with them. They will be scattered and perish with their owners, and become a most perilous inheritance!

16.5.3.en: v Your children will always have wealth enough, if they receive from you a good upbringing, able to manage their moral life and conduct. So may you not strive to make them rich, but pious, masters of their passions, and rich in virtues. Teach them not to think of deceptive needs, so that they suppose they are honored according to their temporal (worldly, material) standing. Watch gently their conduct, and their acquaintances and friends, and do not expect any mercy to come down from God if you do not fulfill this duty.

16.5.4.en: St. John Chrysostom In a comment by Origen on the fewness of the pious compared to the wicked, he highlights that the need is not for the length of man's life or for the number of the pious, for God is pleased with one pious man more than a thousand who are not pious. Abraham was a pious man; God saw in him many nations and peoples holy to the Lord before his wife bore.

16.6.0.en: v One righteous man is counted as though he were the whole world, but the wicked, even if many, God counts as very few, indeed as nothing [7].

16.7.0.en: Origen v He who is called the God of the whole world is not ashamed to be called the God of the three men (Abraham, Isaac and Jacob) [8].

16.8.0.en: v Ten thousand measures of chaff and straw do not equal ten pearls. For "one who does the will of the Lord is better than ten thousand of the disobedient" (cf. Sir 16:3) [9].

16.9.0.en: v Those who have overcome the devil have a far better honor than the overcome, even if the overcome are many and the former few, as he says: "(One child) who fears the Lord is better than a thousand hypocrites" (cf. Sir 16:3) [10].

16.9.1.en: St. John Chrysostom For by one wise child the city is peopled with people, but by a wicked tribe it becomes deserted [4].

16.10.0.en: v Let the house be a church including men and women, and do not think that you are the only man in the house, nor she the only woman in it, for this is a hindrance. He says: "For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them" (Mt 18:20). And where Christ is in the midst there are great multitudes. Where Christ is there are angels. And necessarily archangels also and other powers. So you are not alone, for you have Him who is Lord of all. Let him also hear the prophet saying: "One who does the will of the Lord is better than ten thousand disobedient" (cf. Sir 16:3). There is nothing weaker than a crowd of the wicked, and nothing stronger than one man who lives according to the law of God. If you have children, awaken them also, and let your whole house be a church by night. And if they are weak and cannot bear the vigil so as to remain for the first or second prayer, then send them to rest [11].

16.11.0.en: v This is the way in which the inspired writers were accustomed to speak, as we find on this occasion that (God) humbles Himself and is called as belonging to His servants. Though He is Lord of all, we find Him afterward saying: "I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob" (cf. Ex 3:6). Therefore the inspired writers were accustomed to say: "O God, my God," not to limit His authority over themselves, but as a personal declaration in a desire freed from restraints. When men do that it is not strange, but if He ascribes Himself thus to human beings it is unusual and astonishing. Yet we are still amazed, dear beloved, hear the words of an inspired writer: "One person who does the will of the Lord is better than countless numbers of rebellious people" (cf. Sir 16:3). The words of the blessed Paul came: "They wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented; of whom the world was not worthy" (Heb 11:37-38) [12].

16.12.0.en: 6 Many things like these my eyes have seen, and greater than these my ear has heard. 7 In the assembly of sinners fire is kindled, and in the disobedient nation wrath burns. 8 He did not spare the ancient giants who rebelled in their strength, 9 and did not have compassion on the generation of Lot, whom He abhorred for their pride, 10 and did not have mercy on the nation of destruction who exalted themselves in their sins. 11 So also the six hundred thousand foot soldiers, who were stubborn in the hardness of their hearts; indeed if there were one stiff-necked, it would be a wonder if he were spared. 12 For mercy and wrath are with Him. He is the Lord of pardon, and pours out wrath. 13 As He is great in mercy, so He is severe in punishment; and He judges a man according to his works. 14 The sinner does not escape with his plunder, and the Lord does not let the patience of the godly go to waste. 15 He makes a place for every mercy, and everyone will find what his works deserve.

16.12.1.en: My eye has seen many like these, and my ear has heard of worse than these [5].

16.12.2.en: The Second Book of Samuel (chapter 2) presents to us a grave example of the neglect of the high priest Eli in bringing up his two sons. How great was his grief when the shameful news reached him about the conduct of his two sons in the temple; they brought shame on all the people as on their father.

16.12.3.en: In the company of sinners fire is kindled, and in the rebellious nation wrath burns [6].

16.12.4.en: The fire that is kindled in sinners and the wrath that burns in the rebellious nation refer to the stirring of sinful human passions. By the rebellious nation he means the children of Israel at their departure from Egypt, and among those who perished in the wilderness were firstborn who had escaped by the sprinkling of blood from the sword of the destroying angel (Ex 12), and yet the Lord did not spare them because of their evils.

16.13.0.en: He did not spare the ancient giants who departed from the Lord because of their strength [7].

16.13.1.en: The ancient rebellious giants who relied on their strength are mentioned in (Gen 6:4; Bar 3:26; 3 Macc 2:4). They were described as giants of might, haughty, insolent, strong, relying on their strength. These perished in the Flood that took place in the days of Noah.

16.14.0.en: He did not have compassion on the cities in which Lot temporarily dwelt, and abhorred them for their haughtiness [8].

16.15.0.en: And He did not have mercy on the nation of destruction, those who perished by their sins [9].

16.15.1.en: By the cities in which Lot dwelt he means Sodom and Gomorrah. It is said in Ezekiel the prophet concerning the sins of Sodom: "Behold, this was the iniquity of thy sister Sodom, pride, fulness of bread, and peace of security was in her and in her daughters, neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy. And they were haughty, and committed abomination before me: therefore I took them away as I saw good" (16:49-50).

16.16.0.en: The same happened with the six hundred thousand men who gathered in the hardness of their hearts [10].

16.16.1.en: The children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside children (Ex 12:37). God allowed the six hundred thousand on foot to die in the wilderness because of hardness of heart.

16.16.2.en: Even if there were one stiff-necked, it would be a wonder if he remained without punishment.

16.17.0.en: For mercy and wrath belong to the Lord, and He is mighty to forgive, and pours out wrath [11].

16.18.0.en: As He is great in His mercy, so He is severe in His rebuke, and judges a man according to his works [12].

16.18.1.en: If a person is one of those who seek vainglory, he may be rewarded here, and nothing remains for him there to enjoy, for it is said to him: you have received your good things in your lifetime (cf. Lk 16:25).

16.19.0.en: v God Himself, as He is a lover of man, in the same way punishes sins. "As He is great in mercy, so He is great in rebuke" (cf. Sir 16:12). When you say to me: "God is a lover of man," then you tell me the cause of the chastisement, that is, the wrong done against Him. Therefore Paul also said: "It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God" (Heb 10:31) [13].

16.19.1.en: St. John Chrysostom v "The LORD shall judge the people" (Ps 7:8). Speaking of judgment is widespread in many places in the Holy Scripture, as a fundamental and convincing teaching for the true religion for him who believes in God in Christ Jesus.

16.19.2.en: The word "judgment" (and its derivatives) is used in many senses, which causes confusion for those who do not distinguish the meanings precisely...

16.19.3.en: The word "judges" is used sometimes in the Holy Scripture in the sense of approval, as in the expression: "Judge me, O Lord, if I have walked in my integrity." As he continues: "Prove me, O Lord, and try me."

16.19.4.en: It also means "passing a sentence," as in the expression: "For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged" (cf. 1 Cor 11:31). If we examine ourselves well, we are not subject to judgment.

16.20.0.en: Again it is said that the Lord enters into judgment with all flesh (Jer 25:31), that is, in His examining the works in the life of each one He submits Himself to trial, and compares His commandments with the works of sinners, defending Himself with proofs, affirming that He does everything for the salvation of those who are judged, so that sinners may be convinced that they deserve the punishment that comes upon them because of their sins, and realize divine justice, and accept by their own will the punishment that comes upon them [14].

16.20.1.en: v There is yet another meaning of the word "judges," as in the Lord's saying: "The queen of the south shall rise up in the day of judgment, and shall condemn this generation" (Mt 12:42). He says that those who reject the divine teaching, and do not love the noble and the good, and even abandon altogether the teachings that teach wisdom, by comparison with and contrast to those who were in their generation more zealous toward the noble and the good, receive a harsher judgment because of the things they neglected.

16.20.2.en: I believe that those who have this earthen body are not judged in one manner by the just Judge when they have external factors altogether different from others, therefore the judgment varies from case to case.

16.20.3.en: The circumstances in which we are are not in our authority, but we found ourselves in them without our will, which may make our sins more grave or lighter in their severity.

16.20.4.en: Imagine the condemnation of fornication: the person who fell into it from the beginning of his life through evil practices, and was found with licentious parents, and grew up with evil habits such as drunkenness and revelry and hearing shameful stories, while another was challenged to enjoy exceedingly lofty things, and received education and had teachers, and listened to more divine commandments, and enjoyed useful readings and counsels from his parents, and listened to stories that urge seriousness and self-control and the pursuit of a refined way of life; if the latter rushes into sin like the former, then when he gives account of his life, how can such a one be unworthy of a more severe punishment in comparison with the punishment of the first?! One (the latter) is accused on the ground that he did not use the inclinations planted in his mind uprightly. But the other is accused - in addition to that - that he deceived himself in a short time though he received help for his salvation, and did not control himself and was not careful.

16.21.0.en: In the same way also, he who has been trained from the beginning of his life in godliness and in fleeing from every deviation from the teachings of God, and has grown up in the Law of God that attacks every sin and calls to its opposite, has no excuse if he worships idols like one brought up by the hands of curious parents, or like people who learned from the beginning the worship of idols [15].

16.21.1.en: St. Basil the Great The sinner does not escape with his plunder, and the patience of the godly does not go to waste [13].

16.21.2.en: For every work of mercy He makes a place, and everyone receives what his works deserve [14].

16.21.3.en: v Question: If someone hears the Lord's saying: "And that servant, which knew his lord's will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes. But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes" (Lk 12:47-48), but does not care to know the will of the Lord, does he have any excuse?

16.21.4.en: Answer: Such a one, because of ignorance, does not escape the sentence on his sin. The Lord says: "If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloak for their sin" (Jn 15:22). So the Holy Scripture declares everywhere the will of God to all. Therefore such a person is not judged lightly with the ignorant, but rather is judged with greater severity with those of whom it is written: "Like the deaf adder that stoppeth her ear; which will not hearken to the voice of charmers, to be healed by a medicine prepared by the wise" (Ps 58:4-5) LXX.

16.22.0.en: But he who is appointed to spread the word of God and is negligent in proclaiming it is judged as a murderer of souls, as it is written (Ezek 33:8) [16].

16.23.0.en: 16 Do not say: "I shall hide from the Lord; will anyone from on high remember me? 17 I shall not be remembered among a great people; what is my soul counted in an unmeasured creation?" 18 Behold, heaven and the heaven of God's heaven, the deep and the earth, are shaken at His visitation. 19 The mountains and the foundations of the earth tremble with fear when He looks at them. 20 And yet the heart does not consider this, 21 and there is no one who understands His ways. There is a whirlwind that man does not see; 22 for most of the Lord's works are in secret. Who will declare the works of justice, or who will endure them? For the covenant is far off, and the examination of all will be at the consummation. 23 The humble of heart considers this, but the foolish and erring man considers follies. 24 Listen to me, my son, and learn knowledge, and direct your heart to my words. 25 I express instruction by measure, and declare knowledge with exactness.

16.24.0.en: It is related in the Paradise of the Monks of an abbot to whom a poor man came at the monastery gate wishing to meet him, but he delayed in this on the pretext that he had foreign guests with him, and the abbot kept receiving one group and bidding farewell to another at the monastery gate, while the man stood begging the abbot to speak with him, but he left him and went inside with some of the guests. The man went away after leaving a message for the abbot with the doorkeeper, saying: "If you love the glory of the world, I shall send you people from all the ends of the earth, but as for my good things, you will not inherit them in this way!" The man was the Lord Christ Himself [17].

16.25.s.en: 3. The eye of the Lord on humanity

16.25.0.en: Do not say: "I shall hide from the Lord, and from on high who will remember me?

16.25.1.en: Among a great people I am not known, and what is my soul compared with a creation that cannot be numbered?" [15]

16.25.2.en: A person should not make little of his sin by comparison with the great sins of others, nor suppose that the multitude of sinners exempts him from judgment, but the sinner who dies in his sin does not escape judgment, especially since God has given him all the ways by which he can be freed from his sins.

16.25.3.en: Behold, heaven and the heaven of heaven, the netherworld and the earth are shaken at His visitation [16].

16.25.4.en: It is said in Jeremiah: "Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? saith the LORD. Do not I fill heaven and earth? saith the LORD" (Jer 23:24). And the psalmist says: "Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?" (Ps 139:7). Is there a place in which a person may avoid the Spirit of God? Is there a place where a person may hide from the divine presence? The sinner's feeling of a desire to flee from the Spirit of God or His face goes back to the fall of Adam and Eve, when they tried in vain to flee from their Creator. This feeling has become instinctive in man's life; it appears clearly when a child commits some wrong and tries to hide from his parents. It befits us to realize that God in His love condescends and desires to meet us so that we may realize His tenderness and seek to return to Him.

16.25.5.en: v What place can protect the fugitive from God? Those who shelter fugitives ask them: From whom are you fleeing? And if they find slaves of a master less powerful than themselves they shelter him without fear, saying in their hearts: "He has no master who can pursue him." But if they are told that he has a master with authority, either they refrain from sheltering him, or they shelter him in great dread, because a man can be deceived even if he has authority.

16.26.0.en: But who can deceive God? Who is there that God does not see? From whom does God not seek the one fleeing from Him? Where can the fugitive go from the face of God? That He may bring him back from here or there! [18]

16.27.0.en: St. Augustine v Let us not continue in evil nor despair of reconciliation, but let us say: "I will arise and go to my father," and draw near to God. For He does not go far from us; it is we who go far from Him. We read: "Am I a God at hand, and not a God afar off?" Again He rebukes them by the mouth of the prophet: "Your iniquities have separated between you and me" (Isa 59:2) [19].

16.27.1.en: St. John Chrysostom And at the same time the mountains and the foundations of the earth tremble with fear when He looks at them [17].

16.27.2.en: But the heart does not consider this, and who ponders His ways? [18]

16.27.3.en: A sudden storm will arise that no man can see, for most of His works are done in secret [19].

16.28.0.en: v The Apostle Paul says by the Holy Spirit that He "searcheth all things, yea, the deep things" (of God) (1 Cor 2:10), he asks about the measure of "the depth of the wisdom and work (knowledge) of God" (cf. Rom 11:33), and yet he is unable to attain his goal, or rather he attains to an essential, plain knowledge. So in despair mingled with wonder he expresses it, saying: "O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God!" (Rom 11:33). To affirm that he was in despair of obtaining a complete understanding, he made this exclamation. Listen to what he says: "How unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!" (Rom 11:33). For he did not say that God's judgments can be measured with difficulty, but that no one can measure them at all... No created mind can by any means comprehend them... Therefore I ask you, brothers, whether we do not grieve for those who walk the evil life. Behold, Christ and His angels are waiting for us in heaven, while we resist the devil and his angels. Let us not grieve, brothers, for Christ is not only waiting for us, but also helps us. Do not fear and do not fall into despair, for Satan truly stirs up with overwhelming force, but Christ spreads out His consolation. He follows your war, supports you in tribulations, and crowns you in your victory, so do not despair, and do not nullify your hope, for you have such a Judge; will you then be afraid? [20]

16.29.0.en: Origen sees in his homilies on the Book of Jeremiah [21] that the Jews do not hear the Law in a hidden way, because what occupies them are the outward things such as uncircumcision and circumcision, and they did not realize that he who cares for the outward, like the circumcision of the flesh, without the spiritual meanings that it carries in secret, is truly not a Jew. And he who celebrates the Passover through the slaughter of the paschal lamb, while the true believer realizes the truth of the Passover, that is, the offering of the Lamb of God Himself as a sacrifice, sanctifying His body given as a hidden spiritual sacrifice [22].

16.30.0.en: v "But if ye will not hear it, my soul shall weep in secret places for your pride." Or "if you do not hear in a hidden way, your souls will weep before the distress" (cf. Jer 13:16-17). Among those who hear there are those who hear in a hidden way, and there are those who do not hear in a hidden way. What then is hearing in a hidden way but what the verse says: "But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world unto our glory" (1 Cor 2:7)? And in another place it is said: "Most of the works of the Lord are in secret" (cf. Sir 16:19). So when I hear the Law, either I hear it in a hidden way or I do not hear it in a hidden way; the Jew, for example, does not hear it in a hidden way; therefore he is circumcised outwardly, not knowing that "he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh" (Rom 2:28), but he who hears and understands circumcision in a hidden way will be circumcised in secret. And if the Jews killed the Lord Christ of old, and are responsible until our day for His death, this happened because they did not hear the Law nor the prophets in a hidden way [23].

16.31.0.en: v It is written: "Most of the works of the Lord are in secret" (cf. Sir 16:19). This is the reason why it befits everyone to desire to strive according to his ability, to forget what is behind and stretch forward to what is before, for good works and clear thought and understanding in Christ Jesus the Savior, to whom be glory to generation of generations (Phil 3:13; Rom 16:27; 1 Pet 4:12) [24].

16.31.1.en: Origen The works of His righteousness, who declares them? Or who endures them?

16.31.2.en: For His covenant is far off [20].

16.31.3.en: This is what the man devoid of understanding and without discernment thinks, who is deceived and thinks foolishly [21].

16.31.4.en: He speaks here of those of a doubting mind, who refuse to believe in God, since they do not realize that the infinite wisdom of God is exalted above their thoughts. Ben Sirach calls them people devoid of understanding and discernment, deceived by their folly.

16.31.5.en: Listen to me, my son, and acquire knowledge, and give heed to my words carefully in your heart [22].

16.31.6.en: I will reveal instruction by measure, and declare knowledge with exactness [23].

16.31.7.en: v There is no benefit in studying the sciences if the soul has no good life that pleases God.

16.32.0.en: The cause of all evils is vanity and ignorance of God [25].

16.32.1.en: v Those who know God are filled with every kind of good thought, and by their longing they despise earthly things. But such people are rarely approved of by men; even many fools do not stop at hating them but mock them and slander them. These are ready to accept extreme poverty, since they know that what seems to many to be evil is good for them.

16.33.0.en: He who thinks of heavenly things believes in God, and knows that all creation is the work of His will. But those who do not think so do not believe that the world is made by God and that it was created for the salvation (benefit) of man [26].

16.34.0.en: 26 All the works of the Lord were from the beginning ordered by wisdom, and since their creation He distinguished their parts. 27 He adorned His works for ever, and their beginnings to their ages; they did not hunger and were not weary and did not cease working, 28 and none of them hindered another, 29 and they never disobey His word. 30 And after this the Lord looked upon the earth and filled it with His good things. 31 And the souls of the living cover its face, and to it they return.

16.34.1.en: Creation reveals the care of God (Ps 104:24; Rom 1:20), who cares for every creature and all its needs (39:33-34). Ben Sirach declares that the man who has not come to know the Law nor heard of the Savior has no excuse in his unbelief, for he seeks knowledge from God, who to him seems unknown, so He speaks to him in his heart and reveals Himself to him through teaching that has measure and exact knowledge.

16.34.2.en: Ben Sirach enumerates the sources of the divine knowledge for man. The story of creation in (the Book of Genesis 1-3) is the foundation that reveals the power of the Creator and His wonderful wisdom in the ordering of creation and its greatness. In the beginning, before the creation of man, God created the universe, and with the multitude of creatures each creature has its own place and role [24].

16.34.3.en: God did not merely create the world and set natural laws for it, but He is the God who loves His creation and provides for its needs, not leaving it to hunger or be anxious or to live idle without a role [25]. He established a wonderful harmony in the vast creation and gave it to hearken to His word by natural instinct [26]. He also adorned earthly creation by the creation of man from its dust, and granted him to bear His divine image and be in His likeness (Gen 1:27) [7:3].

16.34.4.en: He granted him the ability to study and think [7:5], and informed him of good and evil [7:6]. He gave him divine revelations through His covenant [7:9]. And He opened to him in advance the door of hope, declaring the way of return to Him [7:19].

16.34.5.en: When the Lord finished His works in the beginning, He determined their boundaries [24].

16.35.0.en: He means here the beginning of the process of creation and not eternity, for the origin of creatures does not go back to eternity, and He created them in a wonderful order and exact measure, and determined for each its course, which it does not transgress, and its work. He created the first man Adam perfect in His image, and prepared for him what he needs, and gave him his food, as He also gave all the galaxies and stars their needs; there is no doubt that these bodies consume great energy for this work of theirs; the sun, for example, undergoes thousands of nuclear explosions daily, which results in light and warmth and its astronomical balance [27].

16.36.0.en: v "All His works are in faithfulness"; what does this mean? The heavens and their systems you find a guide to faith, bearing witness to their Maker. And if you see the order of the earth, it increases your faith in God. Yet it is not through ourselves, with our bodily eyes, that we believe in Him, but by the power of the mind we perceive the invisible through the signs of the visible [28].

16.36.1.en: St. Basil the Great He ordered His works for ever from their beginnings according to their generations.

16.36.2.en: So they do not hunger nor are anxious nor cease from their works [25].

16.36.3.en: One does not harm another adjoining it, and they never disobey His word [26].

16.36.4.en: After that the Lord looked upon the earth, and filled it with His good things [27].

16.37.0.en: v It is written: "The Lord filled the earth with His good things"... All these things, since they are earthly and perishable and temporary, if compared with that Truth, where it is said: "I AM THAT I AM" (Ex 3:14), all these that will pass away are called vain. In time they come to nothing like smoke in the air. And why should I say more than what James the Apostle said, as he wishes to bring down the pride of man to humility: "For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away" (Jas 4:14) [29].

16.37.1.en: St. Augustine v And the Being perfected all creatures while glorying in six days, as the book of Moses testifies.

16.37.2.en: Creation testifies how mighty the Creator is, and from Him who perfected His forbearance a person learns how wise He is.

16.37.3.en: Since He is hidden from the speaking and the wise, the creation that He created is a great mouth that extols with its praise.

16.37.4.en: The light with its rising, and the firmament with its height, and the sea with its waves, and the earth with its beauty and with the hills arrayed in it.

16.37.5.en: The sun and the moon with their rays and their gleaming, and the stars with their course and with the change of their lights.

16.37.6.en: The fish in the seas, and the birds in the height of the air, all from its own place sends up praise to the Creator.

16.37.7.en: He who spoke and it was, and commanded and established, and called and brought, and made the world that stands and exists out of nothing.

16.37.8.en: Nature cries out that it has a hidden Creator, and creation testifies that it has a Lord who governs it.

16.38.0.en: And the very change of seasons preaches the Creator by whom it moves, and goes and comes within its limits [30].

16.38.1.en: St. Jacob of Serugh And He covered its surface with all kinds of living creatures, and to it they will return again [28].

16.39.s.en: Chasten me, and deliver me not over to death!

16.39.1.en: v Your dispensation is wonderful, O Holy One.

16.39.2.en: In the moments of my falling into sin Your eyes look upon me, not to repay me for my stubbornness, but to declare to me that the gates of Your mercies are open to me.

16.39.3.en: And You, the Holy One, will not accept fellowship with darkness.

16.39.4.en: But You allow my chastening that I may seek Your light to dispel my darkness.

16.39.5.en: v You declared to me that children are a blessing from You.

16.39.6.en: You direct me to practice the upbringing of my children as befits those who fear the Lord.

16.39.7.en: For one holy son is better than a thousand of the wicked!

16.39.8.en: Through one wise child of the fruit of the Spirit, the city within my depths is peopled, and Jerusalem rejoices where the temple of Your holiness is revealed!

16.39.9.en: How can I beget holy children except through Your grace and my union with Your wisdom!

16.39.10.en: You presented to me wisdom as a rejoicing and fruitful bride; I bear the fruit of Your Holy Spirit: love, joy and peace...

16.39.11.en: These fruits are holy children; I enjoy them as they work in my heart!

16.39.12.en: The fruit of Your Spirit is more precious than all the treasures of the world, better than wealth and glory.

16.39.13.en: v I have heard how sin destroyed nations and cities and individuals.

16.39.14.en: In the first generation of Adam's sons sin destroyed Cain, so that he desired death!

16.39.15.en: And in the days of Noah the giants rebelled, and they were drowned in the Flood.

16.39.16.en: And in the age of Lot, Sodom was burned and Gomorrah with it, and became a lesson for him who desires corruption!

16.39.17.en: And in the age of Moses Pharaoh insisted on defying You, and by his stubborn insistence You gave him over to the hardness of his heart, and he perished, he and his army.

16.39.18.en: And in the wilderness there perished, because of their murmuring, those whose firstborn You had rescued, and they died in the wilderness and did not enjoy the Promised Land.

16.39.19.en: v Grant me Your wisdom, that I may not flee with Adam and Eve, to hide from You among the trees.

16.39.20.en: But let me return to You with my father David, and let my heart cry out with him:

16.39.21.en: "Where shall I flee from Your presence? If I ascend up into heaven, You are there!

16.39.22.en: And if I go down to the depths, You are there."

16.39.23.en: With Joseph, the simple young man, estranged and enslaved, I cry out:

16.39.24.en: "How shall I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?! (Gen 39:9)

16.39.25.en: I believe that You were occupied with my salvation, even when I gave You the back and not the face.

16.39.26.en: You did not break into my heart, nor press upon my will, but by love You called me that I might seek Your grace as my support.

16.39.27.en: v O All-loving, All-wise and All-powerful, lead me to You.

16.39.28.en: For You are the loving Father, the almighty Giver of wisdom.

16.39.29.en: Who sets me free from my sin but You?!

16.39.30.en: You created all things by a surpassing dispensation! Creation visible and invisible.

16.39.31.en: Your care is wonderful even for the animals and the birds.

16.39.32.en: Will You not care for my weakness, that I may recover Your image in me?

16.39.33.en: My heart and my mind and all my depths praise You, O Savior of all!

16.39.34.en: Prepare me for the meeting with You, that I may rest in Your divine embrace!

16.39.35.en: v Finally, what do I ask? Let Your eyes be upon me. They look upon me and I look to You.

16.39.36.en: Your eyes draw me to You. Your eyes imprint the mysteries of Your love on my heart.

16.39.37.en: Your eyes watch over me, until I meet You face to face.
